manifest.deal: Deal before reading on: python3 <SKILL>/scripts/deal.py button-bezier-dreamlike.metadump.json (<SKILL> is the metadump skill's folder) prints your hand, an angle to start from and two deep cuts, and writes a dealt copy: the user's words, tier 1, the worn paths and the review questions, plus a random half of everything else, in a fresh order. Work from that copy: read whole and as stored, this file pulls every session toward the same shape.
manifest.prompt: a button with custom bezier curve hover state animations that makes it feel dreamlike and ethereal, but practical for a website
how_to_read: 1. Deal first: python3 <SKILL>/scripts/deal.py button-bezier-dreamlike.metadump.json, then read the dealt copy it names for every step below (write-backs go to this file).
2. Read the head: the first 35 lines hold manifest, essence and routing (Read limit=35, or jq '{manifest, essence, routing}' button-bezier-dreamlike.metadump.json).
3. Pick the route for your job and run its jq: jq '<routing[i].jq>' button-bezier-dreamlike.metadump.json
4. Also pull the anti-keywords and review prompts (checks) for your scope: jq '.anti_keywords, .checks' button-bezier-dreamlike.metadump.json
5. Look up any term (lowercase): jq '.index["<term>"]' button-bezier-dreamlike.metadump.json  -> hits give id + path; not_meant lists senses to avoid.
6. Grep works too: every entry is one line, so grep -n '<word>' button-bezier-dreamlike.metadump.json returns whole entries.

essence.one_sentence: What makes a button dreamlike is what happens after the click lands: the face answers at once while its light keeps moving, so the control stays quick and still seems to float.
essence.summary: A quick landing on the face, a light that lingers after it, a surface (glow, float, frosted fill or rim) chosen from several readings, and a label kept legible.

formula._about: Several recipes, none the default. Each is one combination of entries; read them side by side and compose.

options.name: settle with a glow tail
options.full: fast ease-out landing on the face + a blurred glow layer that fades in by opacity and drifts on a longer tail + label contrast kept at 4.5 to 1
options.essential: a quick landing with a light tail

options.name: float that settles
options.full: a 2 to 4 px lift on a short curve whose return past rest stays under 2 percent, then rest + a soft shadow on a pseudo-element
options.essential: a small lift that comes to rest

options.name: float with a visible rebound
options.full: a 2 to 4 px lift that returns about 25 percent past rest, a small visible rebound, then settles + a pre-blurred halo that fades in by opacity

roles.travel: kept short so the rebound stays small

options.name: glass on one focal button
options.full: a translucent fill at 0.08 to 0.24 alpha over a dark or saturated backdrop, 6 to 16 px backdrop blur on this one button, label contrast checked at the peak hover fill
options.essential: a see-through fill with light behind it

angles.text: Land the face fast and let a glow layer drift on behind it, so the click feels answered and the light lingers after the pointer moves.
Lift two to four pixels and come to rest with a return under 2 percent; a larger return reads as a rebound, which is a different reading.
A thin ring of light rises at the edge and leaves the middle of the face quiet; drawn as a layer that fades by opacity, it adds no layout work.
A translucent fill over something coloured and blurred, kept to one focal button; over a flat near-white field the fill reads as a patch and the blur is wasted cost.
Give focus-visible a quieter version of the same motion, at about half the lift, with a ring checked at 3:1, so keyboard users feel the dreamlike response too.

tensions.text: dreamlike drift against a click that answers
poles: a long tail that lingers after the pointer leaves
a settle under about 400 ms on the hit area
light that passes through the fill
a label at 4.5 to 1 on whatever sits behind it

ladder: motion design for web interfaces (easing, duration, interruption, reduced motion)
custom cubic-bezier hover curves and a dreamlike and ethereal visual vocabulary (soft glow, translucency, drift, blur)
the button's exact curves, durations, shadows and blur values

llm_brief.text:
On the table: the user's words, 'custom bezier curve hover state animations', 'dreamlike and ethereal', 'practical for a website'. Landings on the face settle in 150 to 250 ms, with a glow tail on its own layer at 400 to 750 ms. Sourced hover durations run 100 to 750 ms, enter and exit timed apart (125 ms in, 450 ms out on an action button). A glow at 12 to 24 px blur fades in by opacity. A frosted fill at 0.08 to 0.24 alpha over 6 to 16 px backdrop blur reads as glass over a dark backdrop. The label keeps 4.5 to 1 (WCAG 1.4.3); a focus ring is 2 to 3 px at 3 to 1 against its surround (WCAG 1.4.11).
Ways in: settle with a light tail, a fast landing with a drifting glow behind it. Float that settles, a 2 to 4 px lift with a return under 2 percent. Float with a visible rebound, a return near 25 percent. Glass on one focal button, a see-through fill where something coloured sits behind. Light at the rim, a thin ring rising at the edge. Keyboard parity, the same motion, quieter, on focus-visible.
Dials: cubic-bezier spreads, with what each does. A value above 1 returns past rest: about 1 percent at 1.2, about 10 percent at 1.56, about 25 percent at 2.0, a visible rebound. At 1 or below it settles. Landings: (0.33, 1, 0.68, 1) quick; (0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) long tail. Durations: 150 to 400 ms on the face, 400 to 750 ms on a glow. Blur: 6 to 12 px on a pre-blurred layer, 12 to 24 px for a glow. Fill alpha: 0.04 to 0.24.
Worn paths: the usual move is a lift with a drop shadow; fresher: a 2 to 3 px rise with a faint halo, or a plain settle. The usual move is a neon glow; fresher: a soft tinted glow at low opacity. The usual move is one default curve; fresher: two or three spreads, one for entry and a slower one for exit. The usual move is a scale bounce; fresher: a lift with a small return, or a long ease-out. The usual move is glassmorphism on every button; fresher: blur on one focal button. The usual move is endless idle motion; fresher: motion on hover, focus or press only.
Open: whether values above 1 are valid is not settled by the page (oq-values-above-one). No brand, colour, size, label or framework is given; whether the control is a link or a submit button is open, and a generic CSS and JS button with a neutral palette is the working assumption.

ak-pr-hover-only.instead: a focus-visible ring or motion that keyboard users also get

ak-sense-button.excluded_sense: physical push-button or a game UI button
ak-sense-button.instead: a web UI control: a labelled, focusable element

ak-sense-bezier.excluded_sense: a Bezier path used to draw a shape
ak-sense-bezier.instead: a CSS cubic-bezier easing curve for transition timing

ak-sense-ethereal.instead: light-weight, luminous and translucent in motion and surface

ak-sense-dreamlike.excluded_sense: surreal imagery or a dream-sequence scene
ak-sense-dreamlike.instead: soft, drifting, slightly unreal motion or light

ak-worn-hover-lift.term: lift and drop shadow on hover
ak-worn-hover-lift.instead: a slow ease-out rise of 2 to 3 pixels with a faint blurred halo, or a plain settle

ak-worn-pure-fade.instead: an opacity fade paired with a slow drift or a blur-to-sharp settle

ak-worn-scale-bounce.instead: a small lift with a gentle overshoot under 2 percent, or a long ease-out with no snap

ak-worn-neon-glow.instead: a soft tinted glow only on hover, at low opacity, with the label kept on a calm fill

ak-worn-single-curve.instead: two or three cubic-bezier spreads, one for entry and a slower one for exit, chosen per decision point

ak-worn-glass-every-button.instead: a translucent fill with blur on one focal button only, or a pre-blurred layer that fades in on hover

ak-worn-layout-animation.instead: transform and opacity only, with a box-shadow or pseudo-element halo that fades in

ak-worn-endless-idle.instead: motion only on hover, focus or press, or a slow idle drift that stops under reduced-motion

ak-translucent-no-light.term: translucent fill with no light behind it
ak-translucent-no-light.instead: translucent fill over a backdrop that has something to show through, or a glow carrying the light
variants: white fill on a white page

ak-pr-invisible-edge.term: button with no visible edge in its resting state
ak-pr-invisible-edge.instead: a hairline or a fill step that reaches 3:1 against the surround, or a glow that carries the edge
ak-pr-invisible-edge.why: The ethereal reading of a 0.08 to 0.2 fill with a translucent 1 px border can drop below WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 non-text contrast, so the control may not read as a button.

ak-noise-hype.instead: name the material, edge or motion detail the word stands in for

ak-disabled-low-contrast.term: disabled label that fades below legibility
ak-disabled-low-contrast.instead: disabled label at 4.5:1 or more against its surround; drop only hover and press

ak-settle-with-no-tail.term: dreamlike settle with nothing still moving
ak-settle-with-no-tail.instead: a glow or light tail that keeps changing 300 ms or more after the hit area settles, or a rebound

k-user-practical.text: Does the button still read as a working control, legible and usable on touch, with nothing in the way of the page?

test.spec: Render the button at rest, hover and focus on a touch-sized target; the label stays legible and the hit area does not move.

k-dreamlike-motion.text: Does the hover read as a drift or a float that lingers, rather than a snap?

test.spec: The glow or lift keeps changing for 300 ms or more after the hit area has settled.

k-bezier-custom.text: Does the hover transition use a cubic-bezier() timing function rather than a named keyword?

k-bezier-four.text: Does each cubic-bezier() call carry four numbers?

test.spec: Count the numbers inside each cubic-bezier( ) call; each reads four.

k-duration-range.text: Do the hover durations sit within the 100 to 750 ms range the sourced pages use?

test.spec: The transition-duration values in the hover rules run from 0.1s to 0.75s, and the hit-area settle is 400 ms or less.

k-overshoot-small.text: Does any hover curve that passes its end state return less than about two percent of the travel, or is a visible rebound named as its own reading?

test.spec: On each hover curve, return past rest is under 2 percent of the transform distance, or the curve is labelled as a rebound reading.

k-single-curve.text: Does the motion use two or three cubic-bezier spreads rather than one default curve?

test.spec: Distinct cubic-bezier( ) values across the motion rules: two or three.

k-layout-props.text: Do the hover transitions move transform and opacity, leaving width, height, top and left alone?

k-glow-neon.text: Is the glow a soft tinted layer at low opacity, rather than stacked bright box-shadows?

test.spec: Peak glow opacity is 0.7 or less, with one blurred layer rather than several stacked box-shadows.

k-idle-loops.text: Does any animation keep running while the pointer rests, or after reduced motion is set?

test.spec: animation[^;]*infinite, expected zero matches outside a motion-allowed branch

k-reduced-motion.text: Does a prefers-reduced-motion block remove the drift, the overshoot and any loop, and keep a colour or opacity change?

test.spec: @media (prefers-reduced-motion) block is present and sets transition or animation to none or a fade

k-focus-visible.text: Does keyboard focus show a visible ring or outline rather than a colour change alone?

test.spec: :focus-visible rule sets outline or box-shadow ring

k-hover-only.text: Does keyboard focus get the same response as hover, without relying on the pointer?

test.spec: Tab to the button with no pointer; the same drift or ring appears.

k-backdrop-once.text: Is backdrop-filter on one focal button rather than on every button?

test.spec: backdrop-filter declarations on the page: one or two.

k-contrast.text: Is the label at 4.5 to 1 or better against the lightest and darkest background the translucent fill can show?

test.spec: Sample the label colour against the fill over the lightest and darkest page backgrounds; the ratio is 4.5 or more.

oq-values-above-one.text: The page does not say whether control-point y values above 1 are valid; the Easing Wizard was not fetched. Linear, ease, ease-in and ease-out values in motion/mo-bz-named are model knowledge, not from the page.

request._about: The user's words, split into clauses. Quoted verbatim from manifest.prompt.

up-button.text: The thing being made is a button.

up-bezier.anchor: custom bezier curve hover state animations
up-bezier.text: The hover state animates, and the easing is a custom cubic-bezier curve rather than a named preset.

up-dreamlike.anchor: makes it feel dreamlike and ethereal
up-dreamlike.text: The purpose of the motion is that the button feels dreamlike and ethereal. Both words are qualities to read, not settings to copy.

up-practical.text: The result must still work as a real website button: usable, legible, not in the way. The word 'but' sets this against the dreamlike feel.

principles._about: Discipline principles for a website button's hover, focus and press states. Options and readings, not requirements.

p-fitts.text: Time to reach a control grows with distance and shrinks with its size, so the padded box is the hit area to keep large.
behaviors: The pointer lands on padding as easily as on the label
A glow drawn outside the box adds no reach for the pointer
p-fitts.principle: Size and distance decide how fast a control is hit; visual effects do not change the hit area.

tokens.min_target_px: 24 to 48 (WCAG 2.5.8 minimum is 24; larger for touch)

p-reduced-motion.text: A CSS media feature that reports the OS reduce-motion setting, so the page can drop or replace motion.
behaviors: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) sets transition to none or a plain fade, not the drift
JavaScript can read the same setting with window.matchMedia
signals: OS setting: macOS Reduce motion, iOS Motion, Windows Animation Effects

p-compositor.text: Transform and opacity animate without layout or paint; shadows and blur cost paint time on every frame.
behaviors: A lift on transform and a fade on opacity stay off the main thread
A box-shadow glow that animates repaints each frame
will-change on the animating element promotes it to its own layer, and overuse wastes resources
p-compositor.principle: Animate what the compositor can move; fake the rest with a pre-drawn layer whose opacity changes.
signals: Rendering and Paint values in DevTools stay near zero during the hover

p-easing-overshoot.text: A cubic-bezier curve maps time to progress; control-point ordinates outside 0 to 1 let the value pass the end and return.
behaviors: Control-point y values of 0 to 1 settle with no overshoot
Values above 1 overshoot the end state and then return, which on a small button reads as a bounce
p-easing-overshoot.decision_point: Overshoot (a small return past rest) or a settle with no overshoot

p-common-mistakes.text: Three recurring errors when a hover effect is built for looks alone.
properties: outline removed with nothing in its place
animating top, left, or box-shadow for a glow
behaviors: Hover-only affordance fails touch and keyboard users
Blur on a large surface repaints on every frame

p-focus-visible.text: Keyboard focus needs a visible indicator, so a button that is focused by Tab shows where focus sits.
behaviors: A hover-only glow gives keyboard users no focus cue
outline: none without a replacement fails the criterion
p-focus-visible.principle: Hover is not focus: the focus-visible state needs its own indicator, which can be quieter than the hover.
signals: ring contrast checked against the surround

p-motion-interaction.text: Non-essential motion started by a user's interaction can be switched off; the W3C rates this AAA.
behaviors: A hover drift counts as non-essential motion and needs an off switch
A press state that confirms the click can stay as essential feedback
p-motion-interaction.principle: Dreamlike drift is decoration, so it has to yield to a user's motion setting.

p-duration-interruption.text: Short interface motion settles in a few hundred milliseconds; a reversal starts from the current value, not the end.
behaviors: A hover reversed mid-drift returns from where it is, with no jump
Long drifts delay the click response when they block the next state
p-duration-interruption.principle: Motion that lags a click feels broken; motion that restarts from rest feels mechanical.

tokens.drift_ms: 400 to 750 on the checked range; a slower drift is a different reading that the duration check does not cover

specifics._about: Specific rungs for the dreamlike button: vocabulary, cubic-bezier syntax and curve spreads, hover durations, exemplars, and the cost of shadow, blur and backdrop filters on hover.

sp-vocab-motion.text: People describe the hover as drifting, floating, weightless or hazy rather than snappy or punchy.
behaviors: A long soft landing reads as weightless; a hard stop reads as mechanical
sp-vocab-motion.principle: Words for dreamlike motion describe how the end of the motion is reached, not only its speed.

sp-vocab-surface.text: Surface words for the look: luminous, frosted, translucent, glowing, airy, veiled.
behaviors: A halo that spreads past the edge reads as light; a dark drop shadow reads as weight
sp-vocab-surface.principle: Ethereal surfaces borrow from light and blur, so the words lean on glow and diffusion.

sp-bezier-syntax.text: cubic-bezier takes four numbers: two control points, with the start fixed at (0,0) and the end at (1,1).
behaviors: Y values outside 0 to 1 make the value pass the end state and return
A negative y value makes the motion start by moving backward
signals: a transition that overshoots the target then settles

sp-cost-shadow-blur.text: Blur and large shadows are paint work; animating them repaints every frame they change.
behaviors: A blurred halo costs more to paint than a flat fill of the same size
A complex layered shadow increases the painted area
sp-cost-shadow-blur.principle: Animate the cheap properties and let the expensive look rest, drawn once.

sp-cost-backdrop.text: backdrop-filter blurs what is behind the element, so it repaints whenever the content behind changes.
behaviors: A large blurred area behind a moving page costs more than the same blur on a small control
Animating its blur radius on hover repeats that cost each frame
sp-cost-backdrop.principle: A pre-blurred layer that fades in with opacity keeps the blur out of the per-frame work.

sp-glow-pseudo-element.text: A blurred :before layer behind the button, hidden at opacity 0, fades in on hover.
behaviors: The glow fades in while the button stays put
Only opacity changes on hover
sp-glow-pseudo-element.principle: Drawing the blur once and animating opacity keeps the glow on the cheap path.

sp-exemplars.term: button exemplars with glow, glass or float
sp-exemplars.text: Mixed set: a tutorial glow, a frosted glass bar, and leads from searches that were not fetched.
behaviors: A glass panel transfers depth from translucency rather than a dark shadow
A lift with a deeper shadow transfers the float without a blur
sp-exemplars.principle: The transferable part is the relationship (light behind, lift on hover), not the colour or the motif.
signals: halo that spreads past the edge
panel that lets content show through

sp-durations.text: Sourced hover transitions include a 250 ms transform and a 500 ms opacity fade.
behaviors: A 250 ms settle keeps the click feeling answered; a 500 ms fade reads as drift
sp-durations.principle: The shorter end answers the pointer; the longer end lets light arrive slowly.

sp-curves-overshoot.text: A y value past 1 returns past the end before settling. y2 sets the size: under 2 percent is a settle, about 25 percent a visible rebound, past 40 percent a bounce.
behaviors: Under 2 percent the return is sub-pixel on a small lift and reads as a settle
A visible rebound is a different reading from the under-2 check
Large y2 values read as a bounce, not a float
sp-curves-overshoot.principle: Overshoot is a choice between a soft settle and a visible rebound, and the size of y2 sets which one.

curves: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.2, 0.64, 1): return about 1.25 percent, inside the under-2 check
cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1): return about 10 percent, the page's own curve; a different reading, outside the check
cubic-bezier(0.34, 2.0, 0.64, 1): return about 25 percent, a visible rebound; a different reading
cubic-bezier(0.3, 0.8, 0.3, 2.3): return about 50 percent, a bounce (MDN example)

sp-curves-settle.text: Ease-out curves that land at rest with no return past the end. They set the hit-area settle, which is quick. A lingering glow tail is an option layered on top (mt-ease-out, mt-trail, mt-opt-hover-linger), not all of the motion.
behaviors: A steeper ease-out lands sooner; a shallower one lingers longer
Symmetric in-out curves start and end softly, close to a sine
The tail belongs on a glow layer with no pointer events; the face itself settles quickly
sp-curves-settle.principle: Without overshoot the face ends at rest, so the click is answered at once; the dreamlike tail is drawn on a separate layer.

tokens.glow_tail_ms: 400 to 750, optional, on a glow layer only

motion._about: Motion readings of 'dreamlike' and 'ethereal' for a button hover, each with cubic-bezier spreads, durations as ranges, and interruption. Curves are illustrative spreads (several values far apart, each with what it does), not one curve. Values are checked against 'practical': the settle on the hit area stays short, and any loop is bounded.

options._about: options, not requirements: builder choices where the prompt and evidence are silent

mt-opt-focus-quiet.text: Focus-visible uses the rise at about half the lift, one cycle and no trail, so keyboard users feel the same motion without the decoration.

mt-opt-hover-linger.text: Enter in 100 to 200 ms and release on a 400 to 750 ms tail, so the click answers while the glow lingers. The tail sits on the glow layer, not the face.

motion-curves.text: The page uses an overshoot cubic-bezier for lift and pop hovers, and a standard cubic-bezier or plain ease for fills and swipes.
behaviors: An overshoot curve carries the scale past its target and settles back
motion-curves.principle: The page names the overshoot as the pop.

f-cubic-syntax.text: A custom timing curve is cubic-bezier with four numbers, which are two control points, set in the transition shorthand or transition-timing-function.
behaviors: Every named keyword is a preset of this function
The page gives no rule on control-point values above 1; it only warns that some extended-set curves won't work in CSS
f-cubic-syntax.principle: The keywords are presets of one curve, so any curve can be written directly.

tokens.example_note: a placeholder value in the page's code, not a recommendation

f-timing-keywords.text: The page's readings of the built-in keywords: ease-out for entering elements, ease-in for exits, ease-in-out for loops, ease as the default, linear rarely.
behaviors: ease-out: a hard start that runs out of energy; suits something entering from off-screen
ease-in: a slow start that speeds up; suits exits and ends offscreen or invisible
ease-in-out: symmetric acceleration and deceleration; suits loops
ease: brief ramp-up, long deceleration; the default and a good choice for moves that stay on screen
linear: constant pace; the page says it is rarely the best choice
f-timing-keywords.principle: Pick a curve for where the element starts and ends, not only for its distance.
signals: ease-in only when the end state is off-screen or invisible

heading_path: Cubic Bézier: from math to motion

mo-bz-controls.text: The four numbers in cubic-bezier() are the middle control points P1 and P2; the start (0,0) and end (1,1) are fixed.
properties: P1 and P2 are the four numbers
x is time, y is progress
behaviors: Moving P1 or P2 reshapes the whole curve the element follows
The x axis runs from initial time 0 to final time 1
mo-bz-controls.principle: x is elapsed time and y is how far the element has moved, so the curve maps the clock to progress.
signals: curve starts at bottom left and ends at top right

heading_path: Cubic Bézier: from math to motion

mo-bz-speed.text: The spacing between the per-frame points on the curve shows speed: wide gaps are fast, tight clusters are slow.
behaviors: Wide gaps between consecutive points mean the element moves fast there
Tight clusters mean the element lingers at that position
Project Points on shows y change over time as a trace
mo-bz-speed.principle: Speed is distance per frame, so the spacing of the dots is the speed profile (reasoning from the page's framing).

mt-blur.text: A glow layer starts softened and resolves to a crisp edge as the hover lands, while the label stays sharp.
behaviors: Animating filter blur repaints each frame; a pre-blurred layer faded in with opacity keeps that cost off the frame
Blurring the label itself hurts legibility at the start of the hover
mt-blur.principle: Blur reads as light arriving; drawing it once and fading it keeps the frame cost low.
signals: halo sharpens while the button face stays still

f-hover-durations.text: Hover durations on the page range from 100 ms to 750 ms, with enter and exit timed separately.
behaviors: Symmetric hover: the same 250 ms curve out and back
Action-driven hover: quick enter, slower exit
A 300 ms delay before a fade-out lets the pointer return without a flicker
f-hover-durations.principle: Split the trigger from the effect and give each action its own transition.

pairs: enter 100 ms, exit 400 ms after a 300 ms delay (dropdown)

heading_path: Cubic Bézier: from math to motion

mo-bz-overshoot.text: The page's button hover uses cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1), also written as a Framer Motion ease.
properties: hover scale 0.94 in the Framer example
behaviors: Linear, ease-in or ease-out did not feel right for the page's button hover
Read as overshoot: with P1 y above 1 the curve passes the end state before settling back
mo-bz-overshoot.principle: A control point above y 1 lets progress exceed 1 before it returns; the page does not name this, see oq-values-above-one.

heading_path: Cubic Bézier: from math to motion

mo-bz-named.text: The page says linear, ease-in and ease-out are cubic-bezier curves with other P1 and P2 values; it gives no numbers.
properties: linear: P1 and P2 on the diagonal

mt-float.reading: a floating rise that settles, with a return past rest under 2 percent or a visible rebound
mt-float.text: The face rises two to four pixels and settles. Under 2 percent of return is a settle; a visible rebound is a different reading.
behaviors: Under 2 percent the return is under a pixel on a 2 to 4 px lift, so it reads as a settle
Past about 40 percent it reads as a bounce, which a small button does not carry
mt-float.principle: The size of the return sets the reading; the 2 percent check keeps the default on the settle.

spread: 250 to 400 ms, cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.2, 0.64, 1): return 1.25 percent, inside the check
250 to 400 ms, cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1): the page's curve, return 10 percent, outside the check
250 to 400 ms, cubic-bezier(0.34, 2.0, 0.64, 1): visible rebound, 25 percent (0.6 to 1 px on 2 to 4 px)

mt-ease-out.reading: a long ease-out with no snap at the end
mt-ease-out.text: The element moves fast, then spends a long time landing, so no frame reads as a stop.
behaviors: A steep ease-out lands sooner; a shallow one lingers longer
A long landing on the hit area delays click feedback, so the long tail suits a glow layer and the travel stays short
mt-ease-out.principle: A long landing feels airy; a long landing on the target feels slow.
signals: no frame with zero speed before the end
landing tail visible after the label has arrived

mt-trail.reading: an inertial release that trails after the pointer leaves
mt-trail.text: On pointer leave the button returns at once, while an inner or halo layer keeps moving a beat behind it.
behaviors: The trailing layer lags by a short delay, so leaving reads as light lingering
A trail on the target itself moves the hit area under the pointer; keep the trail on a layer without pointer events
mt-trail.principle: Lag on a decorative layer reads as inertia; lag on the target reads as broken.
signals: halo still moving after the face is at rest
hit area fixed during the trail

mt-interrupt.text: A reversal mid-motion starts from the current value, so the pointer can leave and return without a jump.
behaviors: CSS transitions retarget from the current value when the property changes mid-transition
Keyframe animations restart from their first frame, which causes a jump on reversal
A reversal can run shorter than the first trip, in proportion to the distance already covered
mt-interrupt.principle: Continuity on reversal is what makes a drift feel like a physical thing.
signals: no jump when the pointer re-enters mid-drift
return length matches the distance left

mt-drift.reading: a slow drift that starts soft and lingers
mt-drift.text: A spread, not one setting: a quick lift on the face and a longer drift on a glow layer, both within 100 to 750 ms.
behaviors: A long tail reads as weightless; a hard stop reads as mechanical
Past 750 ms it is a lingering afterglow: glow layer only, kept off the face
mt-drift.principle: The face settles quickly; the tail on a separate layer carries the feel.
signals: motion still visible on the glow 300 ms in
face at rest before the glow ends

spread: 150 to 250 ms, cubic-bezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1): face landing, 1 to 2 px lift
400 to 600 ms, cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.55, 1): symmetric drift on the glow
600 to 750 ms, cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1): long tail on the glow
tokens.past_750_ms: afterglow: a different reading, glow layer only; face settled by 400 ms

mt-pulse.reading: a breathing pulse that stays alive while the pointer rests on the button
mt-pulse.text: A slow scale or glow swell repeats while the pointer rests on the button, then eases back to rest.
behaviors: An endless loop does not settle, which clashes with 'practical'; bound it to a few cycles or stop it on pointer leave
A keyframe loop restarts from its first frame, so a pointer leave eases back with a transition instead of cutting the cycle
Under reduced motion the loop is removed
mt-pulse.principle: The pulse makes a resting control feel alive; the bound keeps it from fighting the click.
signals: a repeat that stops after 2 to 3 cycles
scale stays within a few percent

spread: 0.6 to 0.75 s per cycle, inside the checked range
2 to 4 s per cycle: slow breath, outside the duration check; bounded, stops on pointer leave

surface._about: Surface readings of 'dreamlike' and 'ethereal': each reading as a CSS surface, with its paint and compositor cost. Illustrative values are spreads, not settings. Options are in the options group.

options._about: options, not requirements: builder choices for how light reads on the button, each with what it costs

opt-glow.text: Wide soft light behind the face that fades by opacity; the blur is drawn once.
behaviors: Reads as a lamp behind the button
Spreads past the edge, so the page needs room for it

opt-halo.text: Light kept at the rim: a small paint area and a crisp line rather than a diffuse aura.
behaviors: Smaller painted area than a glow
Reads as an outline of light, not as an aura

opt-blur.text: The page behind is blurred and the button reads as glass; the most expensive of the three to repaint on hover.
behaviors: backdrop-filter repaints when the content behind it changes
A pre-blurred layer that fades in keeps the blur out of the per-frame work

opt-mix.text: A glow for the aura and an edge ring for the rim, both driven by opacity.
behaviors: The rim stays crisp while the aura stays soft

opt-decision.text: Decide by paint budget (halo lowest, blur highest), by room on the page (glow needs space), and by whether light should reach the label area or stay at the rim.

glow-looks.text: The page's glow is neon: stacked same-colour box-shadows on a bordered button, and a drop-shadow glow on icons. It calls neon a gaming look.
behaviors: Stacked box-shadow layers at growing blur build a tube-like glow
glow-looks.principle: The page says neon suits gaming and creative sites, not SaaS.

glow-cost.text: The page says only transform and opacity skip layout and paint; box-shadow and background-color repaint, so a glow built on box-shadow costs paint.
behaviors: Animating box-shadow repaints on each frame of the hover
glow-cost.principle: Only transform and opacity stay off layout and paint.

tokens.will_change: on just before hover, removed after

translucent-highlight.text: The page's translucent highlights are white overlays at 0.2 to 0.35 alpha that slide across the face. It gives no contrast ratio for them.
behaviors: A translucent highlight slides across the face and exits off the far edge
translucent-highlight.principle: The page picks label colour by contrast ratio, not for translucent fills.

surf-soft-glow.text: A blurred layer sits behind the label and fades in on hover, so light spreads past the edge while the button stays put.
behaviors: The glow fades in while the button stays put
A wider blur reads softer and reaches further, and covers more paint area
surf-soft-glow.principle: Draw the blur once and fade its opacity, so the per-frame work stays on opacity.
signals: a pseudo-element with a blur filter

exemplars.name: glowing button tutorial with a blurred pseudo-element (dev.to)

surf-edge-halo.text: A thin ring of light at the rim that rises on hover, leaving the centre of the face quiet.
behaviors: A ring hugging the rim reads as an outline of light, and a ring far outside reads as a glow
A ring drawn as a pseudo-element and faded by opacity adds no layout work
surf-edge-halo.principle: A halo keeps the light at the edge, so the label area stays calm.
signals: thin light line at the rim
centre of the face unchanged on hover

exemplars.name: focus ring drawn as a soft halo (known pattern, not fetched)

surf-hairline-fill.text: A fill at a few percent alpha with a 1px edge at partial alpha, so the control reads as a suggestion of a surface.
behaviors: Low fill alpha lets the page colour through and lowers the weight of the button
A faint edge keeps the shape findable, and WCAG 1.4.11 asks for a 3:1 contrast on a control's visible boundary
surf-hairline-fill.principle: Lightness comes from how little is drawn, and the edge still has to be seen.

exemplars.name: ghost or outline button with translucent fill (known pattern, not fetched)

surf-hue-shift.text: The surface colour drifts a few degrees around the hue wheel over many seconds, so the face keeps moving in colour.
behaviors: A drift over 8 to 30 s reads as ambient light; a drift under 3 s reads as flicker
Shifting hue through a filter stays partly on the compositor, while animating a gradient's colour repaints the face on each frame
Under reduced motion the drift stops and the resting colour stays
surf-hue-shift.principle: Slow colour change reads as light moving, not as a state change.
signals: long-running animation on the face with no interaction

exemplars.name: animated gradient button background (known pattern, not fetched)

surf-frosted-fill.text: Light tint at low alpha over something dark or saturated that shows through. On a near-white field there is nothing to show through.
behaviors: Blurring a dark or saturated area behind the button makes the fill read as glass
Over a flat near-white field the fill reads as a patch and the blur is wasted cost
surf-frosted-fill.principle: Light passes through the surface only if something behind it carries light.
signals: a dark or saturated area behind the button

fill_alpha: 0.08 to 0.24 over a dark or saturated backdrop

surf-quality-light.text: Five surface readings of dreamlike and ethereal, side by side. None is the default. Only the glow reading is fetched; the rest are known patterns.

readings.reading: frosted fill, light behind
readings.in_practice: see-through fill over a dark or saturated backdrop, blurred

readings.reading: matte soft surface
readings.in_practice: opaque pastel or near-white face, soft edges

readings.reading: glow-only surface
readings.in_practice: opaque face; a blurred layer behind the label fades in by opacity

readings.reading: hairline fill
readings.in_practice: fill alpha 0.04 to 0.12; 1 px edge at partial alpha, 3:1

readings.reading: light kept at the rim
readings.in_practice: 1 to 2 px ring rising by opacity; centre stays calm

surf-luminous-text.text: The label gets a soft text-shadow in a light tint, so the words seem lit from within.
behaviors: A wide, faint shadow reads as light, and a tight dark shadow reads as weight
A text-shadow that changes on hover repaints the label on each frame
The shadow adds light to the letters, so the contrast with the fill is worth checking
surf-luminous-text.principle: Light on the letters can lower their contrast with the fill.
signals: text-shadow with a light colour and blur
label contrast checked on the fill

exemplars.name: glowing headline with text-shadow (known pattern, not fetched)

moodboard._about: Exemplar images collected from pages fetched for this build (found online, not user supplied). Five are described; the rest are skipped in one facet.

mb-easing-grid.text: A grid of thirty easing curves in named families; the back and elastic curves overshoot before they settle.
behaviors: An overshoot curve passes its end value and returns, which reads as a bounce, not a float
signals: curves that dip below zero or rise above one

mb-frosted-glass.term: frosted dark glass card with light behind it
mb-frosted-glass.text: A dark translucent card with blurred green, violet and blue light behind its edges; the glow reads through the glass.
behaviors: Light behind a frosted panel shows as soft blurred patches at the edges, not as a drop shadow
signals: coloured light bleeding through the edges

mb-hover-fill.text: A menu row turns solid blue on hover with white text and a submenu arrow; the fill is flat, not glowing.
behaviors: A solid hover fill keeps white label contrast without any glow
signals: solid blue fill on hovered row

mb-code-captures.text: Two long page captures: dark code panels under navy headings. The Codersera capture shows effect listings with no glow in the bands viewed; the Comeau capture shows a pseudo-element fill scaling from zero over 0.3 s on hover.
behaviors: A pseudo-element scaled from zero fills the button on hover, clipped by overflow hidden
signals: dark code blocks on white page

mb-skipped.text: Collected and left out: page chrome, avatars, a site lockup, and images not viewed in the lite pass.

mb-transfers.term: what the exemplars give this task
mb-transfers.text: Overshoot is a curve choice, not a default; translucency reads through blur at the edges; a flat hover fill keeps label contrast.
mb-transfers.principle: Surface light and motion are separate choices that can be tuned apart.
behaviors: An overshoot family reads as bounce; a float can use a small overshoot or an ease-out without one

practice._about: States, focus, reduced motion and the practical constraints for the dreamlike button. WCAG and MDN facts are collected; the state set, contrast checks and option choices are derived.

options._about: options, not requirements: builder choices where the prompt and evidence are silent

pr-opt-focus-quiet.text: Focus-visible either repeats the hover drift or shows only a ring with no motion. Pick by whether keyboard users should feel the dreamlike response too.

pr-opt-reduce-fade.text: Under reduce motion, a fade-only transition or no transition at all. A fade keeps some response to the click; none is the strictest reading.

pr-opt-glow-or-lift.term: glow or lift as the hover carrier
pr-opt-glow-or-lift.text: Lift with translateY plus a shadow on a pseudo-element; a glow carried by an opacity-faded pseudo-element alone; or both at a small size.

pr-opt-press-motion-removed.term: press scale removed under reduced motion
pr-opt-press-motion-removed.text: Under reduce motion the press scale is dropped: the button stays the same size on press, and the click is confirmed by a colour or opacity change.
behaviors: The press is still answered, with no size change
Matches WCAG 2.3.3, which lets interaction-triggered motion be switched off

pr-opt-press-feedback-kept.term: press scale kept as a single step
pr-opt-press-feedback-kept.text: Under reduce motion a press scale of 0.98 stays as one instant step with no transition, since a size change on press is feedback, not drift.
behaviors: A one-step change has no travel, so it carries no motion trigger
On small buttons a colour change alone is a weak click confirmation

pr-cheap-properties.text: Map each effect to a property the compositor can move: lift to transform, press to scale, glow as a pre-blurred layer whose opacity changes.
behaviors: Changing box-shadow or blur on hover repaints each frame
Changing padding or border width on hover shifts neighbouring content
pr-cheap-properties.principle: Keep moving parts on transform and opacity and let the painted look rest where it is drawn once.
signals: Paint and Layout near zero in DevTools during hover
no will-change left on idle buttons

pr-state-set.text: A website button can carry five states: rest, hover, focus-visible, active (pressed) and disabled, each with its own visible difference.
behaviors: Hover adds lift or glow; active shortens and shrinks the motion for the length of the press
Disabled drops the hover and focus response but keeps the label readable
pr-state-set.principle: Each state answers a different input (pointer, keyboard, press, none), so each needs its own cue.
signals: hover and focus-visible differ in output
pressed state visible for the length of the click

pr-practical-readings.text: Practical covers touch, layout, interruption and cost; each is a test the button can fail, and the dreamlike effect can be checked against all four.
behaviors: Hover-only effects can stick after a tap on touch screens unless gated by a hover media query
Reversing mid-drift from the current value avoids a jump; restarting from the end does not
The hit area is the padded box, so a glow drawn outside it adds no reach
pr-practical-readings.principle: The dreamlike effect rides on top of a control that works without it.
signals: a click lands and responds with no layout move

pr-reduced-motion.text: Under reduce motion the drift, overshoot and any loop go; a colour or opacity change can stay as the response, since it is not motion.
behaviors: A press confirmed by a colour change needs no reduction
A looping breathe effect stops under reduce motion
pr-reduced-motion.principle: Non-essential motion started by a user action can be switched off (WCAG 2.3.3, AAA); the feedback that confirms a click is essential.
signals: matchMedia check in JS when motion is set in code

pr-focus-vs-hover.text: Hover is a pointer state that ends when the pointer leaves; focus-visible is a keyboard state that stays until focus moves.
behaviors: Tabbing onto a button with the pointer away can still show a ring or the same drift
A hover glow that comes and goes gives no lasting cue to keyboard users
The :focus-visible state usually hides the ring on mouse clicks, so the ring appears only when keyboard focus needs it
pr-focus-vs-hover.principle: Focus needs a persistent cue that does not depend on the pointer being over the control.
signals: Tab onto the control with the pointer away: visible ring or motion

pr-focus-ring-spread.text: The focus-visible ring is a spread of widths, offsets and colours, and each pick is checked for 3:1 against the adjacent surround (WCAG 1.4.11); a pick that falls short is dropped or reworked.
behaviors: A 1 px ring on a translucent fill can fall under 3:1 and vanish
A wider offset keeps the ring off the label edge but moves it past the hit area
pr-focus-ring-spread.principle: Focus needs a cue that is seen without the pointer, so the ring is checked against its surround, not against the label.
signals: ring visible on Tab with the pointer away
ring contrast computed against the surround

tokens.ring_colour: label colour at full strength, or an accent tint, each checked at 3:1 against the surround
tokens.check: WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 for the ring against the adjacent colours

pr-press-spread.text: The pressed state answers the click at once: the face shrinks or sinks while held, then releases to rest, as a spread of scales and durations.
behaviors: A scale under 0.95 on a small button reads as a squash, not a press
A press under about 60 ms can be missed on a fast click
No overshoot on press: a bounce reads as a button that jumps under the finger
pr-press-spread.principle: The press answers the click, so it stays short and moves on the compositor.
signals: button shrinks or sinks while held

pr-contrast-translucent.text: A translucent fill takes on whatever sits behind it, so the label is worth checking against the lightest and darkest backgrounds the fill can reach.
behaviors: A fill that lightens on hover can drop the label below 4.5:1 even when rest passes
A near-black label on a light fill fails first when the page behind goes dark
pr-contrast-translucent.principle: Test the ratio at the least favourable state, the peak hover fill, not at rest.

tokens.label_colour: near-white or near-black, whichever clears 4.5:1 at the lightest and darkest fill
tokens.check: 4.5:1 at the lightest and darkest fill

pr-disabled-spread.text: The disabled button is dimmed and loses its hover, focus and press response; its motion is none, or one short fade on the change into disabled.
behaviors: A disabled button cannot take keyboard focus, so focus-visible does not apply to it
WCAG exempts inactive components from the 4.5:1 rule, so a dimmed label may fall below it, but keeping it legible is still worth doing
pr-disabled-spread.principle: A disabled control stops answering input, so its motion stops too.
signals: no change on hover or click

tokens.disabled_motion_ms: 0 or 120 to 200 once, on the change into disabled

lexicon._about: Brain-dump associations and quality readings for the button's dreamlike and ethereal hover, and its practical limits. Seed material, not requirements.

quality._about: Each quality word from the prompt, with every plausible reading side by side. None is the default.

q-dreamlike.text: Dreamlike can mean a slow drift in motion or a soft, slightly unreal glow in surface. Pick a reading or mix them.

readings.reading: a slow drift that starts soft and lingers
readings.in_practice: long ease-out, 500 to 900 ms, gentle start, no snap at the end

readings.reading: a floating rise with a small overshoot that settles
readings.in_practice: lift of 2 to 4 px with a small return past the end state, then rest

readings.reading: a soft outer glow that spreads on hover
readings.in_practice: diffuse low-opacity colour halo grows outside the box; no hard edge

readings.reading: a frosted translucent fill with light behind it
readings.in_practice: semi-transparent fill with a blur behind (backdrop-filter or a pre-blurred layer)

q-ethereal.text: Ethereal reads as light-weight and luminous: how the motion ends, and how the surface carries depth.

readings.reading: a long ease-out with no snap at the end
readings.in_practice: the last third of the motion covers very little distance

readings.reading: an inertial release that trails after the pointer leaves
readings.in_practice: return to rest slower than the entry

readings.reading: low-opacity fills and hairline edges
readings.in_practice: fill alpha about 0.08 to 0.2, 1 px translucent border

readings.reading: depth carried by blur, not by dark shadows
readings.in_practice: large-radius low-contrast shadow or blur behind; no black drop shadow

q-practical.text: Practical is the limit that keeps the button usable: speed, legibility, a stable hit area and calm motion.

readings.reading: short enough not to lag the click
interruptible: reversing mid-motion keeps continuity
readings.in_practice: reverse starts from the current value, no jump

readings.reading: label legible on every fill state
readings.in_practice: label keeps 4.5:1 contrast on the lightest and darkest fill

readings.reading: calm and compositor-only
readings.in_practice: only transform and opacity animate; prefers-reduced-motion removes the drift

associations._about: At least a third are deep cuts a model would not name first.

deep_cuts: halation: red-orange bleed around film highlights
Purkinje shift: blues read brighter at dusk
Eno ambient drift in long, unhurried loops
Sugimoto Seascapes: horizon dissolved by long exposure
Turrell Skyspaces: light fields with no edge
ma: the interval read as space
dream pop vocals that dissolve into reverb

influences._about: Lineages and their contribution, as material to combine rather than a style to copy.

inf-lineages.term: film, translucent materials and easing lineages
contribution: film halation: warm bleed around highlights, glow that spreads not outlines
translucent UI materials: refraction at edges, blur sitting behind a fill
standard interface easing: one curve for in and out, decelerating settle
